entry.title: Watch what is happening
entry.summary: Notice the movements, sounds, and repeated interests you can actually see. Observation can help you decide whether to make room, offer help, or change something nearby.
entry.cue: When you are unsure what your child is interested in or how much help they need.
detail: Watch what your child reaches toward, returns to, or spends time exploring. Notice their expressions and sounds, and what happens around them. Try to describe these details before deciding what they mean.
You can do this while you are already together. Written notes are one option; both books also make room for simply watching when your hands are full.
Notice your own words and reactions, too. The books use observation to understand an individual child and respond to them, including stepping in when help or protection is needed.

principle.text: Start with what you can see, then consider what it might mean.
